content:
carol.singh: heads up — noticed members of the ADMIN org group still have infra-admin after we renamed the group in Okta earlier today. deprov events in logs but perms remained.

carol.singh: quick repro: rename group "ADMIN" -> "ADMIN-2026" in Okta, wait for delta sync, then check /api/v1/roles?user=... shows infra-admin still active.

scim-sync-bot: delta sync started for org_id=redwood, sync_type=delta, source=okta, run_id=run-2026-03-20-11:02

scim-sync-bot: ERROR: user_remove for user=alice.chen succeeded in idempotency check, but downstream PATCH failed with 409 conflict, queued retry.

dave.kim: 409 on PATCH — that smells like a concurrent write. could be race between group rename flow (DELETE+ADD) and our member removal handler.

alice.chen: i saw the same with two other accounts. after rename, Okta sent separate events: group.update (new displayName) then group.membership.remove. our delta handler seems to process update first, which re-creates mapping and then remove tries to operate on old externalId.

bob.martinez: can you paste the exact SCIM payload we got for the membership remove?

carol.singh: here's the payload from the webhook (sanitized):

```
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
  "Operations": [
    {
      "op": "remove",
      "path": "members[value eq \"00u1abc23def\"]"
    }
  ]
}
```

carol.singh: and the update we got earlier: 
```
{
  "op": "replace",
  "path": "displayName",
  "value": "ADMIN-2026"
}
```

dave.kim: so delta sync shows update then remove. if our sync logic treats group identity by displayName instead of immutable externalId, rename can create a transient group object and membership remove targets old id. we might be doing a PUT to create group then PATCH member removal referencing old id — race.

alice.chen: agree. i think the root cause is our group-keying function. we use group.name for mapping in two places: the SCIM webhook handler and the background group-sync job. group rename paths diverge.

bob.martinez: quick mitigation: add a strong idempotency key on the downstream role-change calls, and block apply if the group externalId mismatch. also consider switching to always-key-by-externalId for delta ops.

carol.singh: filing follow-up tasks: REDW-1298 (investigate rename race + fix mapping), REDW-1299 (retroactive scan for leaked perms from 2026-03-20 10:30->11:15), and REDW-1300 (add idempotency keys to role mutation API). i ran an adhoc audit query and found 6 users with admin perms that should have been removed.

dave.kim: for immediate rollback we should run full sync for org=redwood which will reconcile groups by externalId. scheduling a full sync now, ETA ~12m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

scim-sync-bot: full sync queued (run_id=run-full-2026-03-20-11:12). expected duration ~9m.

alice.chen: after full sync completes let's run the audit script and then revoke any leftover admin roles and post a short postmortem.

bob.martinez: noted. i'll take REDW-1298. alice will own retro scan. carol — can you attach the original Okta events to the ticket?

carol.singh: will do. attaching webhook dump and our sync logs. thanks all. :thumbsup:
